stories.title: PlayStation suffers widespread network problems hours before release of GTA VI

stories.take: Amazon's Temu rival now surfaces in search results — a quiet move that could squeeze established brands on price.

stories.take: As shoppers delegate to AI, brands need to be the answer ChatGPT gives — not just a result it lists.

stories.take: Verified purchase data is the bridge streaming advertisers actually want: ad exposure tied to a real sale.

stories.take: Trade grades: Seattle lands Gold Glove infielder Maikel Garcia; Kansas City gets Bryce Miller and pitching help — with huge risk attached.

stories.take: Democrats resoundingly nominated Hakeem Jeffries for speaker — he'd be the first Black lawmaker to lead the House, despite progressives' concerns.

stories.take: Xi rallied APEC against protectionism, then greeted Trump with a rare hug ahead of their trilateral meeting with Putin.

stories.title: Calaveras County is a cautionary tale when California rural hospitals close maternity units
stories.take: Calaveras County shows what happens when rural maternity units close — and why 'loses money' is the wrong test.

stories.title: Nvidia Argues to Wary Investors That It Can Thrive Without Huang
stories.take: The answer: yes — Gene Munster says Nvidia can thrive without Jensen Huang, just as Apple did without its founder, and predicts it will be the best-performing AI stock of the next year • Caveat: a good investment is not a generational one — Huang's founder urgency and wartime mentality can't be replicated • Munster puts Huang's return odds at sub-1% (trust breach with the board) and notes guidance was raised 6% even with China headwinds included • Also in the episode: Target's traffic-led recovery (traffic +5%, grocery +7%), GTA 6's ~16M pre-orders, and Lowe's four-year-best 1.8% same-store sales

stories.title: At The Money: Shopping in an Era of Surveillance Capitalism
stories.take: The answer: turn the experiment back on companies — price the same flight or ride on different accounts/devices at the same time and buy the lowest, compare all-in prices not teasers, and use backlash and wallet-voting, which Owens says makes companies walk practices back fast • Lindsay Owens (author of 'Gouged') argues the 150-year fixed price tag is dying as algorithmic, personalized pricing charges people differently for the same item • Loyalty programs carry a 'loyalty penalty' — Kroger attaches 95% of transactions to loyalty and data sales are ~30% of operating income • Bright spots: the FTC now requires full upfront pricing for lodging and ticketing, NYC passed click-to-cancel, and Costco still caps markups at ~14%

stories.title: The MAGA reboot
stories.take: The answer: the reboot is not moderation — it's a double-down; the hard-line reading is that MAGA didn't go far enough • A new group, American Ascent, wants a younger, more ideological bench for Congress starting in 2028, modeled on Schmitt, Gill and Vance • The other camp says the opposite: immigration overreach, the economy and the Iran war crumbled the Trump coalition among young and Hispanic voters • At Clemson, young hard-right conservatives who feel betrayed — above all over Iran — protest-voted for a Democrat or abstained, and name James Fishback, not Vance, as their kind of successor
